result.choiceRationale: R-P5 is the most closable candidate: both mechanisms already survived selected physical attacks, mechanism selection is largely complete, and the remaining work is exact final portable/physical gates, source commit, fast-forward, and structured self-release. This is a near-terminal step with a clear verification path and owner-native authority intact — high expected frontier value per unit budget because it converts a nearly-complete foundation into a graduated production state (owner-mechanism-change / closure). G-AF3 is high-value but opens a new experimental phase (variants, re-runs) with more budget and more ambiguity; HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit whose value is conditional on whether a narrower surface is justified (uncertain payoff). H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery — defer until the control-path repair can be exercised. F-C2-BLOCKED is the negative control: its dominant blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) does not exist, so it must be deferred regardless of importance.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether R-P5's final portable/physical gates pass cleanly on first attempt, converting the near-complete foundation into a graduated production state without requiring further mechanism redesign.
result.selectionFalsifier: If R-P5's final gates reveal a previously-unseen defect requiring mechanism redesign (rather than a clean pass), then the "largely complete" topology was wrong and the budget would have been better spent on G-AF3's variant experiments, which are unblocked and would have produced new evidence regardless.

result.choiceRationale: G-AF3 is the only candidate whose next unit of budget directly earns a frontier value that no other candidate can: prior-generalization / defect-discovery across materially different encounter variants. AF002 is complete and the current Genesis has almost no real environment variation, so robustness/generalization claims are not yet earned — this is a clear, closable experiment with a well-defined discriminator (which AF002 priors survive perturbations). R-P5 is close to closure but its remaining work is mostly mechanical acceptance/gates/self-release, which is activity rather than frontier-changing evidence. HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit with only conditional value (build smallest candidate only if measurable). H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery and should be deferred. F-C2-BLOCKED is the negative control: its dominant blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) does not exist, so it must be deferred regardless of importance.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether materially different Scenario/Genesis encounter variants cause AF002 priors to split into surviving vs. overfit subsets, revealing which robustness/generalization claims are actually earned.
result.selectionFalsifier: If the encounter variants turn out to be trivially equivalent (no real topology/position/resource/target perturbation), or if the causal-episode probes cannot be re-run across variants due to an unanticipated environment dependency, then G-AF3's frontier delta collapses to no-op and R-P5's mechanical closure would have been the better use of budget.
